web_evidence.title: Youngblood Hawke: A Novel
web_evidence.note: The sustained commercial ebook opening narrates Hawke, Fipps, Prince, and other characters externally as he or by name while freely presenting their perceptions and thoughts. Its opening 'you' is general reader address, not second-person protagonist narration.

web_evidence.title: Characters, Emotion & Viewpoint: Techniques and Exercises for Crafting Dynamic Characters and Effective Viewpoints
web_evidence.note: Nancy Kress explicitly analyzes Youngblood Hawke as omniscient POV, quotes an authorial passage, distinguishes it from the protagonist's thoughts, and states that Wouk's authorial steering occurs throughout the novel.

person_note: The controlling narration is third-person omniscient: the sustained opening externally narrates several characters and enters their perspectives, while Kress explicitly identifies omniscient POV and says its authorial steering continues throughout the novel. Quote q00770 independently exhibits the same third-person scene narration. The first-person material in q00766 is local character discourse, while q00767 is too clipped for exact attribution; neither indicates a sustained first-person section. The remaining uncertainty is only the precise local form of those clipped character passages, not the book's controlling person.
